title: I am among you as one who serves (Luke 22:24–38)
hookLine: at the table they argue who's greatest, and he tells Peter: I prayed for you

lines: THE BREAD, THE CUP, THE WARNING.
WHICH OF US IS THE GREATEST?
cards: The room might have gone silent. Jesus has just given them bread and said it's his body. He's just said one of them will betray him.
And what happens next, Luke tells us without softening it, is an argument. Over dinner. About which of them is the greatest.

It's almost funny, and painfully familiar: the meeting where everyone angles for credit, the family dinner where old rankings come back out. The friends at this table are doing exactly what people do.

teach.h: KINGS LORD IT; NOT SO WITH YOU.
teach.b: Jesus doesn't shout. He asks a question. Kings lord it over people, he says, and get called benefactors.

teach.h: I AM THE ONE WHO SERVES.
teach.b: Then, in the King James words: "For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am among you as he that serveth."
Everyone knows the answer: the one at the table outranks the one carrying the plates. And Jesus says, I'm the one carrying the plates. The Greek word for serving is the root of the word deacon.
Then he turns to Peter, and his voice changes.

teach.h: ALL OF YOU, SIFTED LIKE WHEAT.
teach.b: "Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat." The King James keeps a detail modern English can't show: in the Greek, that first you is plural.
All of you will be shaken like grain in a sieve.

teach.h: I PRAYED FOR YOU, BEFORE YOU FELL.
teach.b: Then the next line goes singular, just to Peter: "But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren." Peter protests that he's ready to go to prison and to death.
Jesus tells him that before the rooster crows today, he will deny three times that he knows him. Hear the order. The prayer comes before the failure.
Jesus already knows Peter will fall, he has already prayed, and he's already given him a job for afterward: when you've come back, strengthen the others.

how: Churches that have deacons take the title from the same family of Greek words Jesus uses here for serving, and Christians pray for one another by name, especially for people facing a hard test.

o: the head of a church, ranked above the priests
a church servant, from the Greek word for serving
a monk who lives apart in prayer and silence

games.q: what's inside Luke 22:24–38 — tap the pairs.
p: which of them is the greatest

s: the disciples argued about greatness at the last supper
Luke puts the strife right after the bread and the cup.
Jesus prays for Peter only after he denies him
he says he has already prayed, before the denial happens.
Jesus tells Peter what to do after he fails
"when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren."

games.q: Peter has just promised to go with Jesus to prison and to death. Jesus knows he will deny him three times tonight. what does Jesus say to him?
o: tell him to leave before he fails.
tell him you've prayed for him, and to strengthen the others afterward.
say nothing and let it happen.
games.why: "I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren." the prayer and the job come before the fall.

practice: Bring to mind someone heading into something hard, a test, a recovery, a marriage under strain, someone who might not make it through cleanly, and don't rehearse their mistakes.
If you pray, do what Jesus did: pray for them now, ahead of time, that their faith won't fail. If you don't, hold them in good will, and decide now how you'll treat them if they stumble.

wordCard.voice: Deacon. The word rooted in Jesus's claim that at his table, he is the one who serves, carrying the plates instead of sitting to be served.

orig.note: Greek: the one who serves, who waits at table. from the same root as the word deacon.

carryVoice: Your line: I have prayed for you. First the prayer, then the fall, then the way back. Until next time.
